title: Schedule of System Size Limits and Annual Usage Cap — Net Energy Metering
content:
Every Net Energy Metering rider limits the nameplate inverter capacity of the system, in kW AC, and caps the system's expected annual output against the annual usage of the address. The figures below are the rider values the size rule reads.

## Capacity limits and size cap

| Rider | Smallest system (kW AC) | Largest system (kW AC) | Size cap, as a fraction of annual usage | Expected annual output per kW AC (kWh per kW) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | 0.5 | 20.0 | 1.10 (110 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | 0.5 | 25.0 | 1.10 (110 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | 0.5 | 25.0 | 1.50 (150 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | 1.0 | 150.0 | 1.10 (110 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | 10.0 | 1000.0 | 1.00 (100 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | 150.0 | 2000.0 | 1.00 (100 percent) | 1150 |

## Annual usage used for the cap

| Rider | Look-back for annual usage | Address with fewer bills than the look-back |
|---|---|---|
| All six riders | The 12 most recent regular bills | The customer's stated annual load estimate |

The annual usage of the address is the total metered kWh of the 12 most recent regular bills of the service agreement before the application date. Where the address has fewer bills than that, the customer's stated annual load estimate is used instead.

## Reading the schedule

- Expected annual output is the nameplate capacity multiplied by 1150 kWh per kW under every rider.
- The size cap is the rider's fraction multiplied by the annual usage of the address. Under Rider NBT-R the cap fraction is 1.50; under Rider NEM-A and Rider NBT-L it is 1.00, so expected output may equal but not exceed annual usage.
- Hypothetical illustration: an address with 9200 kWh of annual usage under a rider whose cap fraction is 1.10 may host expected output of up to 10120 kWh, which is 1150 kWh per kW multiplied by 8.8 kW AC.
